chunks: And by this chain, from Muhammad ibn Suleyman, from Muhammad ibn Mahfouz, from Abu Al-Maghra'a who said:

I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is nothing more horrible to Iblees and his army than the visitation of the brethren visiting each other regarding Allah.' He said: 'And if two believers meet and they mention Allah, then they mention our merits, the People of the Household, so there would not remain a single lump of flesh upon the face of Iblees except that it would wrinkle, to the extent that his spirit screams for help from the intensity of what he feels from the pain. So the Angels of the sky and the treasurers of the Gardens sense it and they curse him until there does not remain a single Angel of Proximity except that he curses him. So he falls down abased, sorrowful, defeated.'

key_terms.زِيَارَةِ الْإِخْوَانِ فِي اللَّهِ: Visitation of the brethren in Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the effect of believers visiting each other for Allah's sake on Iblees?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the metaphysical impact of 'ziyarat al-ikhan' (visiting brethren for Allah's sake), portraying it as a spiritual weapon that inflicts acute pain upon Iblees and his forces. The narrative emphasizes the centrality of the Ahl al-Bayt in this dynamic, as recalling their virtues alongside divine remembrance amplifies the defeat of Satan, causing the angels to curse him until he is utterly humiliated.
